speedMultiplier.description: How fast the path scrolls and the ball rolls, as a multiple of the game's own (131 px/s down, 252 px/s sideways). Both scale together, so the ball still follows the zigzag path. Applies immediately, mid-run included. Higher values leave less time to tap at each turn.
speedMultiplier.adjustment_guide: The main pace lever. Raise in steps of about 0.1 while the player strings together long runs; lower after runs that end within a few turns, or for relax.

speedRampPerTap.description: Speed-up per tap, in percent of the starting speed. The game's own speed never changes during a run (0); with 1, each tap (turn) adds 1%, so a run speeds up as it goes, up to 2.5x the game's own speed. Each run starts again at speedMultiplier; a change applies to the taps that follow.
speedRampPerTap.adjustment_guide: Keep at 0 for relax and attention. Raise to 0.5-1 for joy and timing, and 1-2 for grit, so long runs get harder as they go. Set it back to 0 if runs keep ending soon after they speed up.

adjustment_instructions:
Mine Rusher is a one-tap endless runner: a ball rolls diagonally along a zigzag path of tiles that scrolls down the screen, and each tap switches its direction (and scores a point). Rolling off the path ends the run (LEVEL_FAILED, with the score); coins are worth 2 points.
Levers: speedMultiplier sets the pace (higher = less time to tap at each turn); speedRampPerTap makes each run speed up as the player taps (higher = long runs get harder faster; 0 = the game's own constant speed).
- relax: speedMultiplier 0.6-0.8, speedRampPerTap 0.
- focus: speedMultiplier 0.9-1.1, speedRampPerTap 0-0.5.
- grit: speedMultiplier 1.2-1.5, speedRampPerTap 1-2; lower speedMultiplier by 0.1 after several runs that end with low scores.
- joy: speedMultiplier 0.8-1.0, speedRampPerTap 0.5-1, so runs build up.
Change one lever at a time, in small steps (speedMultiplier about 0.1, speedRampPerTap about 0.5); runs that end with a score under about 10 mean the game is too hard.
skill_adjustment_instructions:
Mine Rusher trains Timing and Action (tapping at each turn), Perceptual Speed (reading the next turn early) and Attention (staying on the path through long runs).
- timing, action: speedMultiplier 1.0-1.3 with speedRampPerTap 0.5-1, so the timing window shrinks as the run goes on.
- perceptual-speed: raise speedMultiplier gradually (1.2-1.6) with speedRampPerTap 0, so the challenge is reacting in time.
- attention: steady settings (speedMultiplier 0.9-1.1, speedRampPerTap 0) held for long runs; avoid sudden changes.
notes: Mine Rusher's difficulty knobs, matching static/skillprintShim.js, ../parameters.json and GameAdjustmentTester's 'mine-rusher' keys.
